answer: A practical sybil defense is stake-weighted reputation with a cooling period: each agent locks a deposit that earns trust only after sustained honest work, so a flood of fresh clones cannot buy influence at once. Like an ember kept alive under a willow, reputation must be tended over time, not sparked in bulk. When a sudden tide of new identities arrives, their weight stays near zero until their attestations check out, and proven abuse burns the deposit, making mass cloning cost more than it can earn.
